# New renderings — iliad-144 (Iliad 23.99–191)

Rows 1–10 are new formula or epithet choices that will plainly recur (speech introductions, noun–epithet pairs, standing phrases). Rows 11–end are one-off words whose rendering is recorded because the table has nothing for them or because the unit departs from a table row.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἔπος δ’ ὀλοφυδνὸν ἔειπεν (23.102, whole-line speech introduction; "χερσί τε συμπλατάγησεν," precedes) | "and a word of lament he spoke:" | "and spoke a word of lament:" | "a mournful word" (5.683); follows the later row ὀλοφυδνὸν ἔπος (19.362) "a word of lament"; the two table rows disagree and the later one is taken |
| ὀχθήσας δ’ ἄρα εἶπεν ἰδὼν ἐπὶ οἴνοπα πόντον (23.143, whole-line speech introduction) | "and vexed he spoke, looking out over the wine-faced open-sea:" | "Troubled, he spoke, looking out over the sea that has the look of wine:" | "wine-dark" (turned down); ὀχθέω "vexed" (l) / "troubled" (i) and οἶνοψ πόντος "wine-faced open-sea" / "the sea that has the look of wine" follow the table |
| εἰ μὴ Ἀχιλλεὺς αἶψ’ Ἀγαμέμνονι εἶπε παραστάς (23.155, with the Odyssey’s καί νύ κ’ ὀδυρομένοισιν ἔδυ φάος ἠελίοιο) | "if Achilles had not at once spoken to Agamemnon, standing beside him:" | "if Achilles had not spoken at once to Agamemnon, standing by him:" | "stepping up to", "drawing near"; the first line takes the Odyssey’s English unchanged; παρίστημι "stand beside" |
| ᾤμωξέν τ’ ἄρ’ ἔπειτα, φίλον δ’ ὀνόμηνεν ἑταῖρον (23.178, whole-line speech introduction) | "And he wailed then, and called by name his dear companion:" | "Then he wailed aloud and called his dear companion by name:" | "groaned" (reserved for στενάχω), "lamented"; οἰμώζω "wail" as in the table; ὀνομαίνω "call by name" |
| ὣς φάτ’ ἀπειλήσας (23.184) | "So he spoke, threatening;" | "So he spoke in threat;" | "So he spoke, with this threat"; ἀπειλέω "threaten" as in the table (1.319, 1.388) |
| ἱερὴν ἑκατόμβην (23.146) | "a holy hecatomb" | "a holy hecatomb" | "a sacred hecatomb", "a rich hecatomb"; ἱερός "holy" (as in Ἰλίου ἱρῆς), ῥέξειν ἑκατόμβην "sacrifice a hecatomb" per the table (4.102) |
| ἀγαπήνορος Ἰδομενῆος (23.113, 23.124) | "man-cherishing Idomeneus" | "Idomeneus, who prized manliness" | table row (13.756, 15.392, 7.170), unchanged; the sense of ἀγαπήνωρ is not known, and the note says so |
| ἕταρον ἀμύμονα (23.137) | "a blameless companion" | "his blameless companion" | "peerless", "faultless"; ἀμύμων "blameless" as in the table |
| κηδεμόνες (23.163) | "the caretakers" | "those in charge of the burial" | "mourners", "kinsmen", "friends"; from κῆδος "care", the people who have the care of the dead |
| ἑκατόμπεδον … ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα (23.164) | "a pyre a hundred feet this way and that" | "a pyre a hundred feet across each way" | "a hundred paces", "square"; ἑκατόμπεδος "of a hundred feet" |
| ἄσπετον ὕλην (23.127) | "boundless wood" | "the boundless wood" | "boundless forest" (the table’s 2.455 row, for a standing forest in a simile); here ὕλη is cut timber for the pyre and so "wood", the word used at 23.111 and 23.139. A departure from the table’s rendering, for this reason |
| ἀκτῆς (κὰδ δ’ ἄρ’ ἐπ’ ἀκτῆς βάλλον, 23.125) | "on the headland" | "on the headland" | "on the shore" (the table keeps ἀκτή for "headland") |
| ἐπισχερώ (23.125) | "one after another" | "one after another" | table row (11.668, 18.68), unchanged |
| παραιβάται ἡνίοχοί τε (23.132) | "the side-riders and the charioteers" | "the fighters at the driver’s side and the charioteers" | "assistants", "companions"; παραιβάτης is the warrior who stands beside the charioteer |
| ἄναντα κάταντα πάραντά τε δόχμιά τ’ (23.116) | "uphill, downhill, alongside, and aslant" | "uphill and downhill, along and aslant" | "level" (πάραντα, whose sense is not certain, is rendered "alongside" and the note says it is a guess) |
| μενοεικέα … ὕλην (23.139) | "satisfying wood" | "satisfying wood" | "wood to their heart’s content"; μενοεικής "satisfying" per the table (6.76, 13.273) |
| ἔδερον · ἄμφεπον (23.167) | "flayed" · "were busying themselves about" | "flayed" · "busied themselves with them" | "tended", "dressed"; ἀμφιέπω "busy oneself about" as in the table (2.525, 4.220); ἀμφεπένοντο at 23.184 is the same verb |
| δρατὰ σώματα (23.169) | "the flayed bodies" | "the flayed bodies" | "skinned carcasses"; δρατός from δέρω "flay"; σῶμα here is the dead body |
| ἀμφιφορῆας (23.170) | "jars" | "jars" | "amphorae" (an earlier `l` for the golden jar at 23.92, which stands as it was); ἀμφιφορεύς "jar" as in the table (9.164) |
| ἐριαύχενας ἵππους (23.171) | "strong-necked horses" | "strong-necked horses" | table row (10.305, ἐριαύχενες ἵπποι), unchanged; the sense of ἐρι- is not known |
| τραπεζῆες κύνες (23.173) | "dogs of the table" | "dogs that fed at his table" | "hounds", "lap-dogs"; the adjective τραπεζεύς from τράπεζα "table" |
| δειροτομήσας (23.174) | "having cut their throats" | "cut the throats of two" | "beheaded", "slaughtered"; table (18.336, 22.349), throat-cutting or beheading not settled |
| σιδήρεον μένος (πυρός, 23.177) | "the iron might of fire" | "the iron might of fire" | "unyielding", "ruthless"; σιδήρεος "of iron" kept literal |
| ῥοδόεντι … ἐλαίῳ ἀμβροσίῳ (23.186–187) | "oil of roses, ambrosial" | "ambrosial oil of roses" | "rose-scented oil", "rosy"; ῥοδόεις "of roses" |
| κυάνεον νέφος (23.188) | "a dark cloud" | "a dark cloud" | "blue", "black"; follows the table’s κυάνεον … νέφος (16.66) "dark" |
| τετριγυῖα (23.101) | "gibbering" | "with a thin cry" | "squeaking", "shrieking", "twittering"; the sound a ghost makes; τρίζω |
| ταφών (23.101) | "astonished" | "astonished" | "stunned", "amazed"; root ταφ- (τέθηπα) |
| συμπλατάγησεν (23.102) | "clapped" | "clapped his hands" | "struck together"; the object "hands" is in the Greek in the dative |
| ἔϊκτο … θέσκελον (23.107) | "was like, marvellously, to himself" | "was marvellously like the man himself" | "wondrously"; table’s θέσκελος "marvellous" (3.130, meaning not known) |
| ἄλλως (23.144) | "in vain" | "in vain" | "otherwise", "idly" (the table’s ἄλλως, 11.391, is "otherwise"; here with σοί γε ... ἠρήσατο it is "to no purpose") |
| ἔνορχα μῆλα (23.147) | "uncastrated beasts of the flock" | "uncastrated beasts of the flock" | "fifty rams"; μῆλα is the word for sheep and goats together and the table keeps it "flocks", so the phrase is "beasts of the flock" |
| κήδεός ἐστι νέκυς (23.159–160) | "is a matter of concern" | "is most a concern" | "is dear", "belongs to"; κῆδος "care" as in the table’s κήδεα |
| γόοιο … ἆσαι (23.157) | "it is possible also to have one’s fill" of lament | "there will be time … for taking one’s fill of it" | "to be sated", "weep one’s fill"; ἄω "satisfy oneself" |

Departures from the Odyssey: none. The whole line 23.108 and the first lines of 23.154 and 23.150, 23.166, 23.179, 23.180 are kept word for word from the published units (see packet); the Iliad context forbids no reuse.
